definitions.explanation: The highest or most extreme point of something, especially skill, beauty, or achievement. Used to express that something has reached its absolute peak.

examples.english: It is the pinnacle of beauty.

examples.japanese: {職人|しょくにん}{技|わざ}の{極致|きょくち}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: I witnessed the height of craftsmanship.

examples.japanese: この{料理|りょうり}は{和食|わしょく}の{極致|きょくち}と{言|い}っても{過言|かごん}ではない。
examples.english: It is no exaggeration to say this dish is the pinnacle of Japanese cuisine.

notes: Composed of {極|きょく} (extreme, utmost) + {致|ち} (reach, attain). Always expresses something at its absolute highest level — carries a tone of admiration or awe. Common collocations: 〜の{極致|きょくち} (the pinnacle of ~), {極致|きょくち}に{達|たっ}する (to reach the pinnacle), {極致|きょくち}を{極|きわ}める (to attain the ultimate degree). Often used in artistic, cultural, or culinary criticism. Similar to {頂点|ちょうてん} (summit, peak), but {極致|きょくち} has a more literary and evaluative tone, emphasizing the supreme quality rather than just the top position.
